subject: Veridian DPIA: audit scope, EU residency and Art.28 evidence
messages:
From: Luc Moreau <luc.moreau@veridianhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>; procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: DPIA items and Art.28 evidence for EU deployment

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for taking this. We are starting our DPIA for the Veridian pilot and need a short evidence pack that aligns with Article 28/30 requirements and our internal reviewers. Specifically can you confirm the following:

- Can Redwood provide a short formal statement of processing activities (Art.28 statement) that we can include in the DPIA?
- Do you have redacted sample access logs (request/response headers + timestamps) we can review?
- Will processing be confined to an EU region if we select EU deployment? We need an explicit commitment for the DPIA text.
- Any subprocessor roster and KMS description we can attach (high level is OK for first pass).

I attached our DPIA question workbook for context. Ideally we would have draft artifacts by next Wednesday so our legal team can progress.

Thanks,
Luc
Luc Moreau
Head of Security & Privacy, Veridian Health
Attachment: Veridian_DPIA_questions.xlsx

Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPIA items and Art.28 evidence for EU deployment

Hi Luc —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes on an Art.28 processing statement, yes on redacted sample logs, and yes we can commit to EU-only processing when you select the EU region and sign our DPA addendum.

Proposed next steps so we align deliverables with your DPIA schedule:

1) I will share a concise Art.28 statement and a high-level subprocessor roster (redacted for confidentiality) by end of day tomorrow.
2) Irene will prepare a 30-day redacted access-log sample (timestamps + request metadata) and a short note on retention and sampling methodology.
3) Marissa will set a 30-minute DPIA walkthrough to run through our diagrams and KMS approach.

Two quick clarifications for your team:
- Do you need raw request/response headers, or is request metadata + correlation ids sufficient?
- Is a statement that processing is confined to EU region (with SCCs and DPA addendum) acceptable for the DPIA, or do you need additional contractual guarantees (e.g., onshore-only infra)?

I attached our current Redwood processing statement (PDF) for your review. Please tell us if the legal team needs a version with more technical annexes.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_processing_statement.pdf

Thanks — I have a draft pack attached. Key points from the draft:

- Art.28_processor_statement_v1.docx: concise processing activities statement suitable for insertion in a DPIA (includes roles, categories of data, purpose, and retention windows).
- Redacted-access-logs-sample.csv: 30 days of request metadata, with IP and user identifiers hashed; includes correlation ids. Retention policy: 90 days for live logs; 30-day sample provided for review.
- KMS and transfer note: We support customer-managed keys in EU regions via supported KMS providers; full HSM options on dedicated/private deployments.
- Subprocessors: current roster (redacted) attached as a table; our policy is 30-day notice for roster changes and contractual obligations (SCCs/terms) are listed.

Open questions for legal: the customer asks whether our DPA addendum can include an explicit EU-only processing commitment. Practically we can commit to processing in EU region when configured and contractually require SCCs; for onshore-only physical guarantees we should confirm with Infrastructure/GCP/AWS partner teams — that is an ops-level exception.

ETA: I can finalize the documents and hand them to Sofia by EOD tomorrow, pending Ben's confirmation on implications for pricing or required contractual language.

Attachment: Art28_processor_statement_v1.docx; redacted-access-logs-sample.csv

Irene Choi
